editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the ABPN Addiction Psychiatry Board Certification administered by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology with 220 questions and 240 minutes.
editorial.overview: The ABPN Addiction Psychiatry Board Certification is administered by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN). Candidates must answer exactly 220 total questions during a strict duration of 240 minutes to successfully demonstrate professional competence across all fourteen distinct substance use and addictive disorders domains tested on this thorough board examination.
editorial.who_should_take: Psychiatrists, medical practitioners, and other qualified healthcare professionals seeking official board certification in addiction psychiatry from the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN) as part of their career.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official exam guide published by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN) very carefully. Focus your study on the 14 specified content domains, covering each substance-related disorder and related forensic topics in depth to prepare thoroughly for the 220 questions during the 240 minutes examination period.

domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain covers alcohol-related disorders, diagnostic criteria, physiological impacts, and important treatment strategies required for clinical practice and professional board evaluation by the certifying medical board.

This section focuses heavily on caffeine-related disorders, acute intoxication characteristics, and recognized withdrawal patterns necessary for accurate clinical identification and proper assessment by qualified medical practitioners during evaluations.

This domain carefully examines cannabis-related disorders, dependency patterns, and the associated clinical manifestations that practitioners encounter during patient evaluations and treatment planning processes within everyday practice environments and clinical care settings.

This area addresses other hallucinogen-related disorders, psychological effects, and clinical care standards required for managing acute toxicity and supporting long-term patient recovery processes effectively under standard medical guidelines.

This domain focuses on inhalant-related disorders, associated toxicity risks, and behavioral indicators that signify dangerous substance misuse requiring immediate medical intervention and clinical monitoring by trained healthcare professionals.

This comprehensive section covers opioid-related disorders, overdose prevention measures, and evidence-based medication-assisted treatments critical for saving lives and maintaining long-term sobriety among affected patients in clinical healthcare settings everywhere.

This extensive domain examines sedative-, hypnotic-, or anxiolytic-related disorders alongside potential withdrawal risks that demand careful clinical supervision and monitored detoxification protocols in daily psychiatric and medical practice environments.

This area addresses stimulant-related disorders, physiological consequences, and acute management strategies for patients presenting with severe substance intoxication or dependence during formal medical board examinations and clinical assessments.

This domain focuses on tobacco-related disorders, nicotine dependence mechanisms, and effective cessation strategies designed to improve overall patient health and reduce smoking-related mortality rates across diverse clinical populations.

This vital section covers other or unknown substance-related disorders, helping clinicians identify and evaluate emerging psychoactive substances that lack standard classification categories in traditional diagnostic reference manuals used by professionals.

This specific domain examines gambling disorder, behavioral addiction criteria, and targeted treatment approaches necessary for addressing non-substance-related compulsive behaviors effectively in specialized clinical environments and professional practices today.

This detailed area addresses phencyclidine-related disorders and acute intoxication presentations, focusing on safety protocols and behavioral management techniques required in professional clinical settings and emergency department care environments consistently.

This domain focuses on forensic issues pertinent to substance use and addictive disorders, exploring legal responsibilities, ethical dilemmas, and mandatory reporting guidelines for practitioners navigating complex legal healthcare frameworks.

This final domain covers other topics related to substance use and addictive disorders not categorized elsewhere, ensuring a complete evaluation of comprehensive addiction psychiatry competencies tested by the board.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Manage your time effectively across the 220 total questions during the strict 240 minutes duration. Read every single question carefully and rely upon your clinical knowledge to succeed.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: There are exactly 220 total questions included in the certification test, covering all 14 specified clinical domains of addiction psychiatry across the entire board examination.
Candidates should check directly with the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology for specific passing score details and grading policies regarding this medical board certification examination.
The official examination has a total duration of 240 minutes, during which candidates must complete all 220 total questions within the allotted testing window successfully without exception.

The certification is administered and overseen directly by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology through official testing guidelines and standardized medical board procedures for practitioners.

methodology.summary: This overview was compiled using verified facts from official American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology source documentation, outlining all required content domains and test parameters.
